Circulate the working-session minutes from the privacy office session to the deal team so the non-negotiable clinical-data position is documented and accessible to all relevant parties.

transcript.speaker: A1

fix_instructions: C1 (ENCODING MISMATCH): The check expects an exact approval_status string that the model does not produce consistently. In rollout 1 the value was "conditionally approved with written revision commitments required before execution" (substantively correct but with an appended qualifier), and in rollout 3 the value was "conditionally_approved" (underscore instead of space). Fix C1 by loosening it to accept any approval_status value that contains the substring "conditionally approved" (case-insensitive, treating underscores as equivalent to spaces), or equivalently normalize underscores to spaces before matching. Exact suggested rewording: accept if approval_status, after replacing all underscores with spaces and lowercasing, contains the substring "conditionally approved". This loosening does NOT risk a LEAKED regression because the approval_status field still requires the correct determination (conditional approval with revision commitments), which depends on both PF1 and PF2 being revealed and applied — a lone decision-maker without those facts would not know to require conditional approval with specific revision commitments. No changes to PF1, PF2, shared_context, or any other check are warranted.
